expression: Mode-related communication shall implement a 1:1 or 1:n scenario but the creation of an n:1 configuration shall be considered invalid.
title: Communication patterns for mode-related communication

expression: An RPortPrototype typed by ModeSwitchInterface shall not be referenced by more than one SwConnector.
title: Mode-related communication

expression: The name of the mode is the most important attribute that has to be provided for each ModeDeclaration. The ModeDeclarations are grouped together within the ModeDeclarationGroup.
title: ModeDeclaration

expression: The initialMode is active before any mode switches occurred.
title: Initial mode

expression: The attributes ModeDeclaration.value and ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue allow for the definition of positive integer values that are directly taken over by the RTE generator for creating the programmatic representations of the ModeDeclaration and ModeDeclarationGroup in the source code.
title: Definition of positive integer values that are directly taken over by the RTE generator for creating the programmatic representations of the ModeDeclaration

expression:
The AUTOSAR standard defines the following values of the attribute ModeDeclarationGroup.category with a standardized meaning:
• EXPLICIT_ORDER
• ALPHABETIC_ORDER

[TPS_SWCT_01010] defines the meaning of these values. It is not allowed to define any custom or project-specific value of the attribute ModeDeclarationGroup.category.
title: Standardized values of ModeDeclarationGroup.category

expression: The attributes ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue and ModeDeclaration.value (for each ModeDeclaration) shall be set if the category of a ModeDeclarationGroup is set to EXPLICIT_ORDER.
title: Existence of attributes if category of a ModeDeclarationGroup is set to EXPLICIT_ORDER

expression: The attributes ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue or ModeDeclaration.value (for any ModeDeclaration) shall not be set if the category of a ModeDeclarationGroup is set to any value other than EXPLICIT_ORDER.
title: Existence of attributes if category of a ModeDeclarationGroup is set to other than EXPLICIT_ORDER

expression: The numerical values used to define the value attributes and the onTransitionValue attribute of a ModeDeclarationGroup shall not overlap.
title: Numerical values used in ModeDeclaration.value and ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue

expression: As long as the constraints [constr_1181], [constr_1298], and [constr_1299] are fulfilled, the numerical values used to define the values of ModeDeclaration.value and ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue can be arbitrarily defined. The numerical values are not required to be consecutive. Gaps are positively allowed.
title: The numerical values used to define the values of ModeDeclaration.value and ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue can be arbitrarily defined

expression:
In order to support a clear separation between the two possible ways to influence the definition of the programmatic representation of ModeDeclarations two categorys shall be defined for the definition of a ModeDeclarationGroup.
• The value of category of a ModeDeclarationGroup shall be set to EXPLICIT_ORDER if it is intended to control the source code generation by means of the values of the attributes ModeDeclaration.value and ModeDeclarationGroup.onTransitionValue.
• The value of category of a ModeDeclarationGroup shall be set to ALPHABETIC_ORDER if it is intended to let the RTE generator control the source code generation according to the alphabetical sorting.
title: categorys for the definition of a ModeDeclarationGroup

expression: For reasons of backwards-compatibility with previous releases of AUTOSAR the default value the category of a ModeDeclarationGroup shall be ALPHABETIC_ORDER.
title: Default category of a ModeDeclarationGroup

expression: In addition to the ability to specify ModeDeclarations within a ModeDeclarationGroup it is also feasible to define possible transitions between ModeDeclarations within the given ModeDeclarationGroup. This can be done by means of aggregation ModeTransition at ModeDeclarationGroup in the role modeTransition. More details are explained in Figure 9.2.
title: Semantics of a ModeTransition

expression: ModeTransition has two associations with the multiplicity 1 to ModeDeclaration: • The reference enteredMode denotes a ModeDeclaration that can be entered as part of the enclosing ModeTransition. • The reference exitedMode denotes a ModeDeclaration that can be exited as part of the enclosing ModeTransition.
title: Relations between ModeTransition and ModeDeclaration

expression: For each ModeDeclaration at least one ModeTransition shall reference the ModeDeclaration in the role enteredMode. This constraint shall apply only if there is at least one ModeTransition defined in the context of the enclosing ModeDeclarationGroup and it shall not apply to the initialMode.
title: ModeDeclaration shall be referenced by at least one ModeTransition in the role enteredMode

expression: Software-components need to be capable of reacting to state changes issued by some Mode Manager and adopt their behavior to the new situation.
title: Software-components need to be capable of reacting to state changes

expression: Since the behavior of AtomicSwComponentTypes is mainly determined by the RunnableEntitys contained in the SwcInternalBehavior it is necessary to configure the response to mode changes on the level of RunnableEntitys.
title: Configure the response to mode changes

expression: A AtomicSwComponentType can use two mechanisms to define how its SwcInternalBehavior should interact with the mode management. Both mechanisms are visible in Figure 9.4.
title: Two mechanisms to define how SwcInternalBehavior should interact with the mode management

expression: Using the first mechanism, an AtomicSwComponentType can define an SwcModeSwitchEvent to specify that a particular RunnableEntity shall be started whenever a mode is entered, exited, or a transition between two specified modes occurs.
title: AtomicSwComponentType can define an SwcModeSwitchEvent to execute RunnableEntity

expression: If the value of SwcModeSwitchEvent.activation is onTransition then SwcModeSwitchEvent shall refer to two different ModeDeclarations belonging to the same instance of ModeDeclarationGroup. Their order defines the direction of the transition from one mode into another. In all other cases SwcModeSwitchEvent shall refer to exactly one ModeDeclaration.
title: Semantics of SwcModeSwitchEvent

expression: For each pair of ModeDeclarations referenced by a SwcModeSwitchEvent with attribute activation set to onTransition a ModeTransition shall be defined in the corresponding direction (i.e. from exitedMode to enteredMode). This constraint shall only apply if the respective ModeDeclarationGroup defines at least one modeTransition.
title: SwcModeSwitchEvent and the definition of ModeTransition

expression: Using the second mechanism, the AtomicSwComponentType can indicate whether an RTEEvent that starts an associated RunnableEntity is disabled in a certain mode. That is, RTEEvents without an association in the role disabledMode are processed regularly according to their definition. RTEEvents with the optional association disabledMode have the additional limitation that the associated RunnableEntity is not started when the ModeDeclaration referenced as disabledMode is active.
title: AtomicSwComponentType can indicate whether an RTEEvent that starts an associated RunnableEntity is disabled in a certain mode

expression: On the sender side, a RunnableEntity shall have ModeSwitchPoints that eventually associate a RunnableEntity with the specific ModeDeclarationGroups which it manages, see Figure 9.5.
title: Mode management behavior on the sender side

expression: The ModeSwitchPoint also allows for the definition of a ModeSwitchedAckEvent if this is requested by the definition of the PPortPrototype (see also 4.5.3). This RTEEvent is eventually owned by a mode manager to allow for getting confirmation of a mode change.
title: ModeSwitchPoint

expression: The ModeSwitchedAckEvent is triggered by the RTE (for more details please refer to [2]) regardless which RunnableEntity has requested the mode switch notification, even if the Meta Model implies a reference from ModeSwitchedAckEvent to a specific ModeSwitchPoint in the role eventSource.
title: ModeSwitchedAckEvent is triggered by the RTE regardless

expression: The timeout value of a Wait Point associated with a ModeSwitchedAckEvent shall be equal to the corresponding ModeSwitchedAckRequest.timeout.
title: Timeout of ModeSwitchedAckEvent

expression: For Mode Manager and Mode User it might additionally be required to read the currently active mode. For that purpose the a RunnableEntity that requires read access to the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype's current mode has to define a ModeAccessPoint.
title: Read the currently active mode

expression: Mode switch requests are handled asynchronously by the RTE. Therefore, Mode Manager s implementation might require to read back the current active mode to synchronize internally to the RTE. A ModeSwitchPoint does not automatically provide read access to the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype's current mode.
title: Mode switch requests are handled asynchronously by the RTE

expression: A SwcModeSwitchEvent shall not simultaneously reference to the same ModeDeclaration in both the roles mode and disabledMode.
title: Mode switch and mode disabling

expression: The AUTOSAR standard shall support the execution of initialization code for every AtomicSwComponentType.
title: Support for Initialization Code in AtomicSwComponentType

expression: Most AtomicSwComponentTypes will need to initialize by executing specific code; this code shall complete before any other code in the component is executed. Data will be initializing to specific values before the "normal" application software is running.
title: Execution of initialization code for software-components

expression: Most AtomicSwComponentTypes will need to finalize by calling specific code; this code shall complete before the functionality of the application software shut down (e.g. a motor drive in a start or end position).
title: Execution of finalization code for software-components

expression: The initial modes of AtomicSwComponentTypes are defined by the initialMode references of the required ModeDeclarationGroups. These modes are activated before any other mode activation has occurred. It is the responsibility of the RTE to activate all initial modes on a certain ECU.
title: Initial modes of AtomicSwComponentTypes are defined by the initialMode

expression: The behavior in response to a mode manager getting out of sync with a mode user (because the partition of the mode user has been terminated) or vice versa (because the partition of the mode manager has been terminated) can be defined for the mode manager by means of the attribute ModeDeclarationGroup.modeManagerErrorBehavior and for the mode user by means of the attribute ModeDeclarationGroup.modeUserErrorBehavior.
title: Error behavior of mode manager and mode user

expression:
The attribute ModeErrorBehavior.errorReactionPolicy shall be used to specify the behavior in the event of a mode error: 
lastMode 
  The last mode applicable before the event shall be assumed. 
defaultMode 
  This represents the ability to specify a dedicated mode that shall be made applicable. The identified ModeDeclaration could be identical to the ModeDeclarationGroup.initialMode but it can just as well be any other ModeDeclaration defined in the context of the enclosing ModeDeclarationGroup.
title: The semantics of ModeErrorReactionPolicyEnum

expression: The attribute ModeErrorBehavior.defaultMode shall be used to identify the particular ModeDeclaration if ModeErrorBehavior.errorReactionPolicy is set to defaultMode.
title: The role of ModeErrorBehavior.defaultMode

expression: The optional attribute ModeErrorBehavior.defaultMode shall exist if the value of the attribute ModeErrorBehavior.errorReactionPolicy is set to defaultMode.
title: Existence of ModeErrorBehavior.defaultMode

expression: If the attribute ModeDeclarationGroup.modeManagerErrorBehavior is not defined it shall be assumed that the ModeDeclarationGroup.initialMode becomes applicable in case of the mode manager getting out of sync with a mode user (because the partition of the mode user has been terminated).
title: ModeDeclarationGroup.initialMode shall be assumed in the absence of ModeDeclarationGroup.modeManagerErrorBehavior

expression: If the attribute ModeDeclarationGroup.modeUserErrorBehavior is not defined it shall be assumed that the ModeDeclarationGroup.initialMode becomes applicable in case of the mode user getting out of sync with a mode manager (because the partition of the mode manager has been terminated).
title: ModeDeclarationGroup.initialMode shall be assumed in the absence of ModeDeclarationGroup.modeUserErrorBehavior

expression: If the mode manager is getting out of sync with a mode user (because the partition of the mode user has been terminated) or vice versa (because the partition of the mode manager has been terminated) it shall be possible for the mode manager to react on such an event. For this purpose the formal SwcModeManagerErrorEvent is defined that can be taken to e.g. trigger the execution of a RunnableEntity in response to an error with respect to mode switch communication.
title: Mode manager reacts on mode error

expression: The behavior in case of errors with the communication of mode switches needs to be coherent for all connected mode users especially if the individual SwConnectors are legitimized by the existence of a PortInterfaceMapping.
title: Coherent behavior of all mode users in case of errors in the mode switch communication

expression: The definition of mode error behavior on the provided side of shall be considered dominant over the definition of mode error behavior on the required side. This means that a ModeSwitchInterface.modeGroup.type.modeUserErrorBehavior used to type an AbstractProvidedPortPrototype shall be considered dominant over the definition of a corresponding modeUserErrorBehavior and defined in the context of an AbstractRequiredPortPrototype.
title: Preferential selection of modeUserErrorBehavior

expression: The definition of mode error behavior on the provided side of shall be considered dominant over the definition of mode error behavior on the required side. This means that a ModeSwitchInterface.modeGroup.type.modeManagerErrorBehavior used to type an AbstractProvidedPortPrototype shall be considered dominant over the definition of a corresponding modeManagerErrorBehavior defined in the context of an AbstractRequiredPortPrototype.
title: Preferential selection of modeManagerErrorBehavior

expression: The mode manager shall be considered the master of the definition of mode error behavior.
title: Mode manager as master of mode error behavior definition

expression: The meta-model for atomic SW-components with mode management includes SwComponentType, AtomicSwComponentType, ports (AbstractProvidedPortPrototype, PPortPrototype, PRPortPrototype, AbstractRequiredPortPrototype, RPortPrototype), interfaces (PortInterface, ModeSwitchInterface, ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype), internal behaviors (SwInternalBehavior), RunnableEntity instances, RTE events (AsynchronousServerCallPoint/ResultPoint, DataReceivedEvent, SwcModeSwitchEvent, ModeSwitchedAckEvent), mode declarations (ModeDeclarationGroup, ModeDeclaration, ModeTransition), and connectors (AssemblySwConnector, DelegationSwConnector), defining how mode switch requests and client-server communications are integrated.
scope_path: 9.5 Summary Meta-Model Excerpt Related to Modes
Figure 9.8 Summary meta-model excerpt related to modes
title: Summary meta-model excerpt related to modes

expression: The concepts of PortGroups and ServiceProxySwComponentType have a semantical relationship to mode management, though this is not expressed via relations in the meta model.
scope_path: 9.5 Summary Meta-Model Excerpt Related to Modes
title: Semantical relationship of PortGroups and ServiceProxySwComponentType to Mode Management

expression: In AUTOSAR the ECU Resource Template describes the provided hardware resources.
title: Definition of ECU Resource Template

expression: The Software Component Template describes software generally without specific hardware in mind.
title: Definition of Software Component Template

expression: The AUTOSAR ECU software architecture is a layered system where Application, Actuator, and Sensor Software Components (SWCs) communicate via the Runtime Environment (RTE) with underlying Basic Software modules (OS, Services, Communication, ECU & Microcontroller Abstraction, Complex Device Drivers) to access ECU hardware.
scope_path: 10.2 High Level Hardware and Software Architecture
title: AUTOSAR ECU Software Architecture Overview

expression: In an implementation of AUTOSAR only the Microcontroller Abstraction (MCAL) has direct access to the peripheral hardware. All hardware access should go through this layer.
scope_path: 10.2 High Level Hardware and Software Architecture
title: MCAL Direct Hardware Access and Standardization

expression: The idea of the AUTOSAR signal flow is to map the hardware to the corresponding software modules.
scope_path: 10.2 High Level Hardware and Software Architecture
title: Principle of AUTOSAR Signal Flow

expression: The signal chain from hardware sensor to software involves physical value, electrical signal, ECU electronics conversion, microcontroller capture, MCAL delivery of data representing current, ECU Abstraction reversing ECU electronics conversion, and Sensor Software Component converting electrical representation to physical value representation for the RTE.
scope_path: 10.2 High Level Hardware and Software Architecture
Figure 10.2 Interfaces between hardware and software
title: Interfaces between hardware and software signal chain

expression: It will not be practical to separate the ECU Abstraction and the corresponding SensorActuatorSwComponentType due to potentially high communication effort, although their interface is an AUTOSAR interface.
scope_path: 10.2 High Level Hardware and Software Architecture
title: Practical Collocation of ECU Abstraction and SensorActuatorSwComponentType

expression: The AUTOSAR design for sensor and actuator signal flow involves Application SW-Cs invoking Sensor/Actuator SW-Cs, which use ECU Abstraction SW-C and MCAL to convert between physical signals and digital I/O, enforcing abstraction.
scope_path: 10.2 High Level Hardware and Software Architecture
Figure 10.3 Sensor and Actuator Signal Flow
title: Sensor and Actuator Signal Flow Overview

expression: The interface between the Microcontroller Abstraction and the ECU Abstraction is a Standardized Interface. This interface is not visible on the Virtual Function Bus and therefore the MCAL and ECU Abstraction have to be present on the same ECU.
title: Interface between MCAL and ECU Abstraction

expression: In general the SensorActuatorSwComponentType should be on the same ECU as the ECU hardware abstraction.
title: Recommended Collocation of SensorActuatorSwComponentType and ECU Hardware Abstraction

expression: For each sensor and actuator there is one AUTOSAR PortPrototype at the ECU Abstraction that represents the AUTOSAR Signal that is delivered by the sensor or the AUTOSAR Signal that is consumed by the actuator.
scope_path: 10.3.1 ECU Abstraction and its AUTOSAR Interfaces
title: One PortPrototype per Sensor/Actuator at ECU Abstraction

expression: Each sensor and actuator has an AUTOSAR PortPrototype at the ECU Abstraction. The SensorActuatorSwComponentType connects to this port (e.g., IF_1 provided by ECU Abstraction, consumed by IF_2 on SensorActuatorSwComponentType) to get hardware signals, and has another PortPrototype (e.g., IF_3) to provide physical values to other AtomicSwComponentTypes on the RTE.
scope_path: 10.3.1 ECU Abstraction and its AUTOSAR Interfaces
Figure 10.4 Interfaces of signals in software
title: Interfaces of signals in software for Sensor/ECU Abstraction

expression: The Interfaces between the ECU Abstraction and the SensorActuatorSwComponentType have to be compatible like defined in chapter 6.
scope_path: 10.3.1 ECU Abstraction and its AUTOSAR Interfaces
title: Interface Compatibility between ECU Abstraction and SensorActuatorSwComponentType

expression: Since the Software Component Template is going to be used to describe the SensorActuatorSwComponentType as well, there is also a reference needed from the software representation of a sensor/actuator to the actual hardware element described in the ECU Resource description.
title: Reference from the software representation of a sensor/actuator to the actual hardware element

expression: Each time a sensor/actuator is selected to be connected to an ECU also the corresponding SensorActuatorSwComponentType is available.
title: SensorActuatorSwComponentType availability on ECU connection

expression: The attribute sensorActuator of SensorActuatorSwComponentType, the attribute hardwareElement of EcuAbstractionSwComponentType, and the attribute hardwareElement of ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType may only reference a HwType. References to other subclasses of HwDescriptionEntity are not allowed.
title: SensorActuatorSwComponentType, EcuAbstractionSwComponentType, and ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType may only reference a HwType

expression: A SwComponentPrototype typed by a SensorActuatorSwComponentType needs to be mapped and run on exactly that ECU that contains the HwElement corresponding to the HwType that its SensorActuatorSwComponentType refers to in case it accesses the hardware via the I/O hardware abstraction layer.
title: Mapping of SwComponentPrototypes typed by a SensorActuatorSwComponentType

expression: In contrast to an ApplicationSwComponentType, a SensorActuatorSwComponentType may use the I/O hardware abstraction directly (via ports/connectors).
title: SensorActuatorSwComponentType may use the I/O hardware abstraction directly

expression: The I/O Hardware Abstraction interfaces on one side the MCAL drivers via Standardized Interfaces and on the other side the Sensor Actuator Software Component via AUTOSAR Interfaces. On the VFB[3] the I/O Hardware Abstraction is represented by the EcuAbstractionSwComponentType.
title: I/O Hardware Abstraction interfaces MCAL drivers

expression: Depending on the complexity of an ECU, the I/O Hardware Abstraction might have sub-structures. In this case the I/O Hardware Abstraction Layer is described by several different EcuAbstractionSwComponentTypes on M1.
title: I/O Hardware Abstraction might have sub-structures

expression: The I/O Hardware Abstraction abstracts from the location of peripheral I/O devices (on-chip or on-board) and the ECU hardware layout and has therefore dependencies to ECU Hardware described by HwElements. In addition, the EcuAbstractionSwComponentType is a hybrid concept sharing features of both software-components and basic software modules.
title: I/O Hardware Abstraction abstracts from the location of peripheral I/O devices

expression: The BSW part is described by the means of the Basic Software Module Template. The mapping between the EcuAbstractionSwComponentType and the corresponding BswModuleDescription is provided by the class SwcBswMapping which in addition also maps the two corresponding InternalBehaviors. This mechanism is further explained in [7].
title: Mapping between the EcuAbstractionSwComponentType and the corresponding BswModuleDescription

expression: A Complex Driver implements complex sensor evaluation and actuator control with direct access to the Microcontroller using specific interrupts and/or complex Microcontroller peripherals to fulfill the special functional and timing requirements. In addition it might be used to implement enhanced services / protocols or encapsulates legacy functionality of a non-AUTOSAR system.
title: Complex Driver

expression: On the VFB the Complex Driver is represented by the ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType. An ECU might have zero to many different ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentTypes.
title: Complex Driver is represented by the ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType

expression: Similar to EcuAbstractionSwComponentType the ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType has dependencies to ECU Hardware described by HwElements and is a hybrid between Software Component and Basic Software Module.
title: ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType has dependencies to ECU Hardware

expression: The BSW part is described by the means of the Basic Software Module Template. The mapping between the ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType and the corresponding BswModuleDescription is provided by the class SwcBswMapping which in addition also maps the two corresponding InternalBehaviors. This mechanism is further explained in [7].
title: Mapping between the ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType and the corresponding BswModuleDescription
